items.title: Physically irreducible representation (PIR)
items.text:
Let \((\Gamma, \mathrm{Span}_{\mathbb{C}} \{ \mathbf{v}_{i} \}_{i=1}^{d} )\) be a unitary (projective) irrep of group \(G\). Then, its conjugate (projective) representation is \((\Gamma^{\ast}, \mathrm{Span}_{\mathbb{C}} \{ \mathbf{v}_{i}^{\ast} \}_{i=1}^{d} )\). There are three cases for \(\Gamma\) and \(\Gamma^{\ast}\):

  1. \(\Gamma\) is real: \(\Gamma\) and \(\Gamma^{\ast}\) are equivalent and can be taken as real matrices.
  2. \(\Gamma\) is pseudo-real: \(\Gamma\) and \(\Gamma^{\ast}\) are equivalent but can be taken as real matrices.
  3. \(\Gamma\) is not equivalent to \(\Gamma^{\ast}\).

We sometimes need to restrict irrep under a vector space over \(\mathbb{R}\) (instead of \(\mathbb{C}\)), which is called physically irreducible representation (PIR) Stokes et al., 1991.

items.title: Finite group
items.text:
These cases are classified with Frobenius-Schur indicator:

\[ \begin{aligned} \frac{1}{|G|} \sum_{ g \in G } \chi(g^{2}) = \begin{cases} 1 & \mbox{($\Gamma$ is real)} \\ -1 & \mbox{($\Gamma$ is pseudo-real)} \\ 0 & \mbox{($\Gamma$ is not equivalent to $\Gamma^{\ast}$)} \\ \end{cases}. \end{aligned} \]

items.title: Space-group representations
items.text:
Let \(\Gamma^{(\mathbf{k}, 0)}\) and \(\Gamma^{(\mathbf{k}, 1)}\) be representations of space group \(\mathcal{G}\) with \(\mathbf{k}\) vector. Let \(\mathcal{T}\) be a translational subgroup of \(\mathcal{G}\). Consider coset representatives of little group of \(\mathbf{k}\) over \(\mathcal{T}\):

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}} = \coprod_{ \{ i \mid \mathbf{S}_{i} \in \overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}} \} } (\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{w}_{i}) \mathcal{T}. \end{aligned} \]

Then sum over translations in \(\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}\):

\[ \begin{aligned} \frac{1}{|\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}|} \sum_{ g \in \mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}} } \chi^{\mathbf{k}}(g^{2}) &= \frac{1}{N} \sum_{ \mathbf{t} } \sum_{ \{ i \mid \mathbf{S}_{i} \in \overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}} \} } \chi^{\mathbf{k}}\left( (\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{t})(\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{w}_{i}) (\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{t})(\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{w}_{i}) \right) \\ &= \frac{1}{N} \sum_{ \mathbf{t} } \sum_{ \{ i \mid \mathbf{S}_{i} \in \overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}} \} } \chi^{\mathbf{k}}\left( (\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{t} + \mathbf{S}_{i}\mathbf{t})(\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{w}_{i})^{2} \right) \\ &= \left( \frac{1}{N} \sum_{ \mathbf{t} } e^{-i \mathbf{k} \cdot (\mathbf{t} + \mathbf{S}_{i}\mathbf{t}) } \right) \left( \sum_{ \{ i \mid \mathbf{S}_{i} \in \overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}} \} } \chi^{\mathbf{k}}\left( (\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{w}_{i})^{2} \right) \right) \\ &= \mathbb{I}\left[ 2\mathbf{k} \equiv \mathbf{0} \right] \cdot \sum_{ \{ i \mid \mathbf{S}_{i} \in \overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}} \} } \chi^{\mathbf{k}}\left( (\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{w}_{i})^{2} \right), \end{aligned} \]

where \(\mathbb{I}[C]\) takes one if the condition \(C\) is true and takes zero otherwise 1.

items.title: (1) \(\Gamma\) is real
items.text:
The following construction is based on Ref. Inui et al., 1996.

In this case, since \(\Gamma\) and \(\Gamma^{\ast}\) are equivalent, there exists a symmetric unitary matrix with

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{\Gamma}(g) \mathbf{U} &= \mathbf{U} \mathbf{\Gamma}(g)^{\ast} \\ \mathbf{U}^{\dagger} \mathbf{U} &= \mathbf{1} \\ \mathbf{U}^{\top} &= \mathbf{U}. \end{aligned} \]

We impose \(\det \mathbf{U} = 1\) additionally to specify the intertwiner uniquely. The intertwiner can be numerically computed as shown in here.

The symmetric unitary matrix \(\mathbf{U}\) can be diagonalized with real orthogonal matrix \(\mathbf{S}\) as \(\mathbf{U} = \mathbf{S}^{-1} \mathbf{\Omega} \mathbf{S}\) 2. For this symmetric unitary matrix \(\mathbf{U}\), we can choose its square root with

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{T} &:= \mathbf{S}^{-1} \mathbf{\Omega}^{1/2} \mathbf{S} \\ \mathbf{T}^{2} &= \mathbf{U} \\ \mathbf{T}^{\dagger} \mathbf{T} &= \mathbf{1} \\ \mathbf{T}^{\top} &= \mathbf{T}. \end{aligned} \]

A transformed representation \(\mathbf{\Gamma}'(g) := \mathbf{T}^{-1}\mathbf{\Gamma}(g)\mathbf{T}\) is real because

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{\Gamma}'(g) &= \mathbf{T}^{-1} \mathbf{U} \mathbf{\Gamma}(g)^{\ast} \mathbf{U}^{-1} \mathbf{T} \\ &= \mathbf{T} \mathbf{\Gamma}(g)^{\ast} \mathbf{T}^{-1} \\ &= \mathbf{\Gamma}'(g)^{\ast}. \end{aligned} \]

items.title: (2, 3) \(\Gamma\) is pseudo-real or not equivalent to \(\Gamma^{\ast}\)
items.text:
In these cases, we can transform conjugated basis pair to real vectors by unitary matrix:

\[ \begin{aligned} (\mathbf{v}_{1}, \cdots, \mathbf{v}_{d}, \mathbf{v}_{1}^{\ast}, \cdots, \mathbf{v}_{d}^{\ast}) \mathbf{U} &= \sqrt{2} (\mathrm{Re}\, \mathbf{v}_{1}, \cdots, \mathrm{Re}\, \mathbf{v}_{d}, \mathrm{Im}\, \mathbf{v}_{1}, \cdots, \mathrm{Im}\, \mathbf{v}_{d}) \\ \mathbf{U} &:= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\begin{pmatrix} \mathbf{1}_{d} & -i \mathbf{1}_{d} \\ \mathbf{1}_{d} & i \mathbf{1}_{d} \\ \end{pmatrix} \quad (\mathrm{Unitary}) \\ \mathbf{U}^{-1} \begin{pmatrix} \mathbf{D}(g) & \\ & \mathbf{D}(g)^{\ast} \end{pmatrix} \mathbf{U} &= \begin{pmatrix} \mathrm{Re}\, \mathbf{D}(g) & \mathrm{Im}\, \mathbf{D}(g) \\ -\mathrm{Im}\, \mathbf{D}(g) & \mathrm{Re}\, \mathbf{D}(g) \\ \end{pmatrix} \quad (g \in G) \end{aligned} \]

items.title: PIR of space group \(\mathcal{G}\)
items.text: To construct PIR of space group from small representation \(\Gamma^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}\) at \(\mathbf{k}\) Stokes et al., 2013, we apply the finite-group recipe above to the little group \(\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}\). So that the construction remains valid when \(2\mathbf{k} \not\equiv \mathbf{0}\), spgrep (as of v0.6.0) enlarges the carrier from \(\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}\) to the little group \(\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}\bar{\mathbf{k}}}\) of \(\pm\mathbf{k}\) following Stokes et al., 2013; this matches the presentation used by the Bilbao Crystallographic Server.

items.title: Little group \(\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}\bar{\mathbf{k}}}\) of \(\pm\mathbf{k}\)
items.text:
Define the little co-group of \(\pm\mathbf{k}\) as the set of point-group operations that stabilize \(\{ \mathbf{k}, -\mathbf{k} \}\) as a set:

\[ \begin{aligned} \overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}\bar{\mathbf{k}}} := \left\{ \mathbf{S} \in \overline{\mathcal{G}} \;\middle|\; \mathbf{S}^{\top} \mathbf{k} \equiv \pm \mathbf{k} \pmod{\mathbf{K}} \right\}. \end{aligned} \]

By construction, any \(\mathbf{S}\) stabilizing \(\mathbf{k}\) also stabilizes \(\{ \mathbf{k}, -\mathbf{k} \}\), so \(\overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}} \subseteq \overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}\bar{\mathbf{k}}} \subseteq \overline{\mathcal{G}}\). The little group of \(\pm\mathbf{k}\) is its preimage under the point-group projection,

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}\bar{\mathbf{k}}} := \left\{ g = (\mathbf{S}_{g}, \mathbf{w}_{g}) \in \mathcal{G} \;\middle|\; \mathbf{S}_{g} \in \overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}\bar{\mathbf{k}}} \right\} = \coprod_{ \{ i \mid \mathbf{S}_{i} \in \overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}\bar{\mathbf{k}}} \} } (\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{w}_{i}) \mathcal{T}, \end{aligned} \]

with \(\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}} \subseteq \mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}\bar{\mathbf{k}}} \subseteq \mathcal{G}\). When \(2\mathbf{k} \equiv \mathbf{0}\) we have \(\mathbf{k} \equiv -\mathbf{k}\), so \(\overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}\bar{\mathbf{k}}} = \overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}}\) and \(\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}\bar{\mathbf{k}}} = \mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}\) automatically, so \(\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}\bar{\mathbf{k}}}\) gives a uniform domain regardless of whether \(2\mathbf{k} \equiv \mathbf{0}\).

items.title: Real form on \(\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}\)
items.text:
Case (1): \(\Gamma^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}\) is real. Averaging the finite-group intertwiner of (1) over translations, and using \(2\mathbf{k} \equiv \mathbf{0}\) (which holds whenever \(\Gamma^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}\) is real) to collapse the translation sum via \(2\mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{t} \in \mathbb{Z}\):

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{U} &:= \frac{1}{N} \sum_{ \mathbf{t} } \sum_{ \{ i \mid \mathbf{S}_{i} \in \overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}} \} } \mathbf{\Gamma}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}\left( (\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{t})(\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{w}_{i}) \right) \mathbf{B} \mathbf{\Gamma}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}\left( (\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{t})(\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{w}_{i}) \right)^{\ast \dagger} \\ &= \sum_{ \{ i \mid \mathbf{S}_{i} \in \overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}} \} } \mathbf{\Gamma}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}\left( (\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{w}_{i}) \right) \mathbf{B} \mathbf{\Gamma}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}\left( (\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{w}_{i}) \right)^{\ast \dagger}. \end{aligned} \]

Feed this \(\mathbf{U}\) through the \(\mathbf{T} = \mathbf{U}^{1/2}\) step of the finite-group (1) subsection to obtain the real form.

Cases (2, 3): \(\Gamma^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}\) is pseudo-real or not equivalent to \(\Gamma^{\mathbf{k}\alpha \ast}\). Apply the block-diagonal identity from the finite-group (2, 3) subsection with \(g \in \mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}\). For a translation \((\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{t}) \in \mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}\) the block form reduces to a planar rotation:

\[ \begin{aligned} \tilde{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}( (\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{t}) ) = \begin{pmatrix} \cos (\mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{t}) \mathbf{1}_{d} & -\sin (\mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{t}) \mathbf{1}_{d} \\ \sin (\mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{t}) \mathbf{1}_{d} & \cos (\mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{t}) \mathbf{1}_{d} \\ \end{pmatrix}. \end{aligned} \]

items.title: Extension to \(\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}\bar{\mathbf{k}}}\)
items.text:
When \(\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}\bar{\mathbf{k}}} \neq \mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}\), fix any \(a \in \mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}\bar{\mathbf{k}}} \setminus \mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}\) so that \(\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}\bar{\mathbf{k}}} = \mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}} \sqcup a \mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}\) (note \(a^{2} \in \mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}\)). Extending \(\mathbf{\Gamma}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}\) from \(\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}\) to \(\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}\bar{\mathbf{k}}}\) is structurally identical to the co-representation construction in corep: take \(\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}\bar{\mathbf{k}}}\) in place of the magnetic group, \(\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}\) in place of its unitary subgroup, \(a\) as the antisymmetry coset representative, and let the role of complex conjugation be played by the anti-linear action \(\mathbf{k} \to -\mathbf{k}\), so that the conjugated irrep is \(\overline{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}(h) = \mathbf{\Gamma}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}(a^{-1} h a)^{\ast}\) (trivial factor system).

The Frobenius-Schur indicator

\[ \begin{aligned} \xi^{\alpha} := \frac{1}{|\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}|} \sum_{h \in \mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}} \chi^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}((ah)^{2}) \quad \in \{ -1, 0, 1 \} \end{aligned} \]

selects the block-matrix form of \(\tilde{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}(a)\); see corep for the three cases and their derivation. In every case \(\tilde{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}(a h) = \tilde{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}(a) \tilde{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}(h)\) on the remaining coset \(a \mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}\).

items.title: Realification of the corep on \(\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}\bar{\mathbf{k}}}\)
items.text:
Reuse the change of basis from the finite-group \((2, 3)\) subsection and write \(\tilde{\mathbf{D}}(g) := \tilde{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}(g)\). For \(g \in \mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}\) the corep acts \(\mathbb{C}\)-linearly, so on the doubled basis it is block-diagonal and the realification is the same formula as the finite-group \((2, 3)\) subsection:

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{U}^{-1} \begin{pmatrix} \tilde{\mathbf{D}}(g) & \\ & \tilde{\mathbf{D}}(g)^{\ast} \\ \end{pmatrix} \mathbf{U} = \begin{pmatrix} \mathrm{Re}\, \tilde{\mathbf{D}}(g) & \mathrm{Im}\, \tilde{\mathbf{D}}(g) \\ -\mathrm{Im}\, \tilde{\mathbf{D}}(g) & \mathrm{Re}\, \tilde{\mathbf{D}}(g) \\ \end{pmatrix} \quad (g \in \mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}). \end{aligned} \]

For \(g \in a\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}\) the corep acts \(\mathbb{C}\)-antilinearly as \(\mathbf{v} \mapsto \tilde{\mathbf{D}}(g) \mathbf{v}^{\ast}\). On the doubled basis \((\mathbf{v}_{1}, \cdots, \mathbf{v}_{d}, \mathbf{v}_{1}^{\ast}, \cdots, \mathbf{v}_{d}^{\ast})\) this antilinear action is the \(\mathbb{C}\)-linear block-off-diagonal matrix \(\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} \mathbf{0} & \tilde{\mathbf{D}}(g) \\ \tilde{\mathbf{D}}(g)^{\ast} & \mathbf{0} \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)\), since \(g\) exchanges the \(\mathbf{v}\) and \(\mathbf{v}^{\ast}\) blocks of basis vectors while complex-conjugating coordinates. Conjugating with \(\mathbf{U}\) gives

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{U}^{-1} \begin{pmatrix} \mathbf{0} & \tilde{\mathbf{D}}(g) \\ \tilde{\mathbf{D}}(g)^{\ast} & \mathbf{0} \\ \end{pmatrix} \mathbf{U} = \begin{pmatrix} \mathrm{Re}\, \tilde{\mathbf{D}}(g) & -\mathrm{Im}\, \tilde{\mathbf{D}}(g) \\ -\mathrm{Im}\, \tilde{\mathbf{D}}(g) & -\mathrm{Re}\, \tilde{\mathbf{D}}(g) \\ \end{pmatrix} \quad (g \in a\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}). \end{aligned} \]

The corep multiplication law (with \(\ast\) applied iff the left factor is antilinear) is reproduced by ordinary matrix multiplication of these \(2d \times 2d\) real blocks, so the resulting matrices form a real linear representation of \(\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}\bar{\mathbf{k}}}\).

  1. Here we use \(\mathbf{S}_{i}^{\top} \in \overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}}\) as

    \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{1}{N} \sum_{ \mathbf{t} } e^{-i \mathbf{k} \cdot (\mathbf{t} + \mathbf{S}_{i}\mathbf{t}) } &= \frac{1}{N} \sum_{ \mathbf{t} } e^{-i (\mathbf{E} + \mathbf{S}_{i})^{\top} \mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{t} } \\ &= \mathbb{I} \left[ (\mathbf{E} + \mathbf{S}_{i})^{\top} \mathbf{k} \equiv \mathbf{0} \right] \\ &= \mathbb{I} \left[ \mathbf{k} + \mathbf{S}_{i}^{\top} \mathbf{k} \equiv \mathbf{0} \right] \\ &= \mathbb{I} \left[ 2\mathbf{k} \equiv \mathbf{0} \right]. \end{aligned} \]

    ↩

  2. For symmetric unitary matrix \(\mathbf{U}\), if \(\mathbf{v}\) is eigenvector of \(\mathbf{U}\), its conjugacy \(\mathbf{v}'\) is also eigenvector. Thus, we can take real part or imaginary part of \(\mathbf{v}\) as a new basis vector. ↩

items.title: Irreps of space group
items.text: This page formulates little group, small representation, and irreducible representations (irreps) of space groups.

items.title: Reciprocal lattice and transformation
items.text:
Let \(\mathbf{A} = (\mathbf{a}_{1}, \mathbf{a}_{2}, \mathbf{a}_{3})\) be basis of \(L_{\mathcal{T}}\), which is lattice of translational group \({\mathcal{T}}\). We choose basis of the (crystallographic) reciprocal vectors as

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{B} &= (\mathbf{b}_{1}, \mathbf{b}_{2}, \mathbf{b}_{3}) = A^{-\top} \\ \mathbf{b}_{i} \cdot \mathbf{a}_{j} &= \delta_{ij}. \end{aligned} \]

When basis vectors \(\mathbf{A}\) is transformed to \(\mathbf{A}' := \mathbf{AP}\),

  • its dual basis vectors in reciprocal space is transformed from \(\mathbf{B}=\mathbf{A}^{-\top}\) to \(\mathbf{B}' := \mathbf{B}\mathbf{P}^{-\top}\).

  • symmetry operation \((\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{v})\) is transformed to

    \[ \begin{aligned} (\mathbf{P}, \mathbf{0})^{-1} (\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{v}) (\mathbf{P}, \mathbf{0}) = (\mathbf{P}^{-1}\mathbf{RP}, \mathbf{P}^{-1}\mathbf{v}). \end{aligned} \]

  • Coefficients of reciprocal vector \(\mathbf{k} = 2 \pi \mathbf{B} \mathbf{k}_{f}\) is transformed to \(\mathbf{k}_{f}' := \mathbf{P}^{\top} \mathbf{k}_{f}\).

items.title: Irreps of translation subgroup
items.text:
Consider the following irreps of translation subgroup \(\mathcal{T}\) of space group \(\mathcal{G}\),

\[ egin{aligned} \Gamma^{(\mathbf{k})} ((\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{t})) = \exp \left( -i \mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{t} ight) \quad ( \mathbf{t} \in L_{\mathcal{T}} ), \end{aligned} \]

where \(L_{\mathcal{T}}\) is a lattice formed by \(\mathcal{T}\). Let \(L_{\mathcal{T}}^{\ast}\) be a reciprocal lattice of \(L_{\mathcal{T}}\). We can confine \(\mathbf{k}\) within or the surface of a primitive cell of the reciprocal space because, for \(\mathbf{g} \in L_{\mathcal{T}}^{\ast}\), \(\Gamma^{(\mathbf{k})} = \Gamma^{(\mathbf{k} + \mathbf{g})}\). Any Bloch function with \(\mathbf{k}\)

\[ egin{aligned} \Psi_{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{r}) = e^{ i \mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{r} } u_{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{r}), \end{aligned} \]

where \(u_{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{r})\) is periodic with \(L_{\mathcal{T}}\), can be taken as (one-dimensional) basis of \(\Gamma^{\mathbf{k}}\):

\[ egin{aligned} (\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{t}) \Psi_{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{r}) &= \Psi_{\mathbf{k}}( (\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{t})^{-1} \mathbf{r}) \ &= e^{-i\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{t}} \Psi_{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{r}). \end{aligned} \]

We write point group of space group \(\mathcal{G}\) as \(\mathcal{P}\). For \((\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{v}) \in \mathcal{G}\), \((\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{v}) \Psi_{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{r})\) is Bloch function with \(\mathbf{Rk}\):

\[ egin{aligned} (\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{t}) (\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{v}) \Psi_{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{r}) &= (\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{v}) (\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{R}^{-1}\mathbf{t}) \Psi_{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{r}) onumber \ &= \exp \left( -i \mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{R}^{-1} \mathbf{t} ight) (\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{v}) \Psi_{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{r}) onumber \ &= \exp \left( -i \mathbf{Rk} \cdot \mathbf{t} ight) (\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{v}) \Psi_{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{r}) \quad ( ecause \mathbf{R} \in O(3) ). \end{aligned} ag{1} \]

Be careful the basis for calculating inner product in Eq. (1), when you use crystallographic coordinates 1:

\[ egin{aligned} \mathbf{v} &=: \mathbf{A} \mathbf{v}_{f} \ \mathbf{A}^{-1} \mathbf{R} \mathbf{A} &=: \mathbf{R}_{f} \quad \in \mathrm{SL}(3) \ (\mathbf{k}, \mathbf{R}^{-1} \mathbf{v}) &= (\mathbf{R} \mathbf{k}, \mathbf{v}) onumber \ &= 2 \pi \left( ( \mathbf{A}^{ op} \mathbf{A}^{-1} ) \mathbf{R}_{f} ( \mathbf{A}^{ op} \mathbf{A}^{-1} )^{-1} \mathbf{k}_{f}, \mathbf{v}_{f} ight) onumber \ &= 2 \pi \left( \mathbf{R}_{f}^{ op} \mathbf{k}_{f}, \mathbf{v}_{f} ight) \quad ( ecause \mathbf{R}_{f}^{ op} = \mathbf{A}^{ op} \mathbf{R}^{-1} \mathbf{A}^{- op} ). \end{aligned} \]

items.title: Little group
items.text:
Let \(\mathcal{P}\) be point group of space group \(\mathcal{G}\). We define little co-group of \(\mathbf{k}\),

\[ \begin{aligned} \overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}} = \left\{ \mathbf{R} \in \mathcal{P} \mid \mathbf{Rk} \equiv \mathbf{k} \right\}, \end{aligned} \]

where \(\equiv\) is up to reciprocal vectors in \(L_{\mathcal{T}}^{\ast}\). When we use crystallographic coordinates w.r.t. primitive basis vectors, the condition \(\mathbf{Rk} \equiv \mathbf{k}\) is written as

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{Rk} \equiv \mathbf{k} \Longleftrightarrow \mathbf{R}_{f}^{\top} \mathbf{k}_{f} - \mathbf{k}_{f} \in \mathbb{Z}^{3}. \end{aligned} \]

Because lattice \(L_{\mathcal{T}}\) is invariant with \(\mathbf{R} \in \mathcal{P}\), we obtain

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{R} \mathbf{k}_{1} \equiv \mathbf{k}_{2} \Rightarrow \overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}_{2}} = \mathbf{R} \overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}_{1}} \mathbf{R}^{-1}. \end{aligned} \]

When we decompose point group \(\mathcal{P}\) as

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{P} = \coprod_{i=1}^{q} \mathbf{P}_{i} \overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}_{1}}, \end{aligned} \]

\(\mathbf{P}_{i}\mathbf{k}_{1} \equiv \mathbf{k}_{i}\) with star of \(\mathbf{k}_{1}\), \(\left\{ \mathbf{k}_{1}, \dots, \mathbf{k}_{q} \right\}\).

We define little group (of the first kind) of \(\mathbf{k}\) as

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}} = \coprod_{ \{ i \mid \mathbf{S}_{i} \in \overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}} \} } (\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{w}_{i}) \mathcal{T}, \end{aligned} \]

where \(\mathcal{G} = \coprod_{i} (\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{w}_{i}) \mathcal{T}\). We can decompose space group \(\mathcal{G}\) as

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{G} = \coprod_{i=1}^{q} (\mathbf{P}_{i}, \mathbf{x}_{i}) \mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}_{1}}. \end{aligned} \]

Then, for Bloch function \(\Psi_{\mathbf{k}_{1}}(\mathbf{r})\), \((\mathbf{P}_{i}, \mathbf{x}_{i}) \mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}_{1}} \Psi_{\mathbf{k}_{1}}(\mathbf{r})\) is Bloch function for \(\mathbf{k}_{i}\). Thus, our task to calculate irreps of \(\mathcal{G}\) is boiled down to calculating irreps of little group \(\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}\), which is called small representation.

items.title: Projective representation
items.text:
A projective representation of group \(G\) is a non-singular matrix function \(\Delta\) on \(G\) if it satisfied the following conditions: For each group product \(G_{k} = G_{i}G_{j}\), there exists scalar function \(\mu\) (factor system) such that

\[ \begin{aligned} \Delta(G_{i}) \Delta(G_{j}) = \mu(G_{i}, G_{j}) \Delta(G_{k}), \end{aligned} \]

and

\[ \begin{aligned} \mu(G_{i}, G_{j}G_{k}) \mu(G_{j}, G_{k}) = \mu(G_{i}G_{j}, G_{k}) \mu(G_{i}, G_{j}) \quad \mbox{(cocycle condition)}. \end{aligned} \]

items.title: Small representation
items.text:
Let \(\Gamma^{\mathbf{k}}_{p}\) be irrep of \(\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}}\), for \(\mathbf{S}_{i} \mathbf{S}_{j} = \mathbf{S}_{k}\),

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{\Gamma}^{\mathbf{k}}_{p}((\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{w}_{i})) \mathbf{\Gamma}^{\mathbf{k}}_{p}((\mathbf{S}_{j}, \mathbf{w}_{j})) = \exp \left( -i \mathbf{k} \cdot ( \mathbf{w}_{i} + \mathbf{S}_{i} \mathbf{w}_{j} - \mathbf{w}_{k} ) \right) \mathbf{\Gamma}^{\mathbf{k}}_{p}((\mathbf{S}_{k}, \mathbf{w}_{k})). \end{aligned} \]

Then, Simplifying by

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{\Gamma}^{\mathbf{k}}_{p}((\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{v})) &=: \exp \left( -i \mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{v} \right) \mathbf{D}^{\mathbf{k}}_{p}((\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{v})) \\ \mathbf{D}^{\mathbf{k}}_{p}((\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{w}_{i})) \mathbf{D}^{\mathbf{k}}_{p}((\mathbf{S}_{j}, \mathbf{w}_{j})) &= \exp \left( -i \mathbf{g}_{i} \cdot \mathbf{w}_{j} \right) \mathbf{D}^{\mathbf{k}}_{p}((\mathbf{S}_{k}, \mathbf{w}_{k})), \end{aligned} \]

where

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{g}_{i} &= \mathbf{S}_{i}^{-1} \mathbf{k} - \mathbf{k} \\ &= 2 \pi \mathbf{B} \left( \mathbf{S}_{i, f}^{\top} \mathbf{k}_{f} - \mathbf{k}_{f} \right) \quad (\mathbf{S}_{i, f} = \mathbf{A} \mathbf{S}_{i} \mathbf{A}^{-1}). \end{aligned} \]

If we choose origin such that \((\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{t}) \in \mathcal{G}\), \(\mathbf{D}^{\mathbf{k}}_{p}((\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{t})) = \mathbf{1}\) and $\exp \left( -i \mathbf{g}{i} \cdot (\mathbf{w}} + \mathbf{t}) \right) =\exp \left( -i \mathbf{g{i} \cdot \mathbf{w} \right) $ hold. Then, it is sufficient to consider on \(\overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}}\),

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{D}^{\mathbf{k}}_{p}(\mathbf{S}_{i}) \mathbf{D}^{\mathbf{k}}_{p}(\mathbf{S}_{j}) = \exp \left( -i \mathbf{g}_{i} \cdot \mathbf{w}_{j} \right) \mathbf{D}^{\mathbf{k}}_{p}(\mathbf{S}_{k}) \end{aligned} \]

Here, \(\mu_{\mathbf{k}}(S_{i}, S_{j}) := \exp \left( -i \mathbf{g}_{i} \cdot \mathbf{w}_{j} \right)\) holds the cocycle condition and \(\mu_{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{E}) = 1\). Now, our task is to enumerate projective irreps of little co-group \(\overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}}\) with factor system \(\mu_{\mathbf{k}}\).

When we use crystallographic coordinates, the factor system is written as

\[ \begin{aligned} \mu_{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{S}_{j}) &= \exp \left( -i (\mathbf{g}_{i}, \mathbf{w}_{j}) \right) \\ &= \exp \left( -2 \pi i (\mathbf{S}_{i, f}^{\top} \mathbf{k}_{f} - \mathbf{k}_{f}, \mathbf{w}_{j, f}) \right) \quad (\mathbf{w}_{j} =: \mathbf{A} \mathbf{w}_{j, f}). \end{aligned} \]

  1. We interchangeably denote an inner product of two vectors as \(\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}\) or \((\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{b})\). ↩

items.title: Spin representation
items.text: A spin representation is a projective representation with a factor system for spinor wave functions. Here, we give the convention to choose the factor system for spinor in spgrep.

items.title: Symmetry operation of the first kind
items.text:
The map \(\mathrm{SO}(3) i \mathbf{R}_{ heta\hat{\mathbf{n}} } \mapsto \mathbf{U} ( \mathbf{R}_{ heta\hat{\mathbf{n}} } ) := \exp \left( - rac{i}{2} heta \hat{\mathbf{n}} \cdot \mathbf{\sigma} ight) \in \mathrm{SU}(2)\) is not surjective, where \(\mathbf{\sigma}_{i} \, (i=x,y,z)\) are Pauli matrices

\[ egin{aligned} \mathbf{\sigma}_{x} = egin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \ 1 & 0 \ \end{pmatrix}, \mathbf{\sigma}_{y} = egin{pmatrix} 0 & -i \ i & 0 \ \end{pmatrix}, \mathbf{\sigma}_{z} = egin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \ 0 & -1 \ \end{pmatrix}. \end{aligned} \]

In fact, \(\mathbf{R}_{ heta\hat{\mathbf{n}}}\) and \(\mathbf{R}_{2\pi - heta, -\hat{\mathbf{n}}}\) represents the identical rotation. However they gives different unitary matrices with opposite signs. We choose either of the unitary matices for each rotations as convention. In particular, we choose \( heta=0\) for identity \(\mathbf{E}\). We define a factor system from the ambiguity as

\[ egin{aligned} \mathbf{U}(\mathbf{R}) \mathbf{U}(\mathbf{R}') =: z(\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{R}') \mathbf{U}(\mathbf{R}\mathbf{R}') \quad (\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{R}' \in \mathrm{SO}(3)). \end{aligned} \]

In our convention, \(z(\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{R}) = z(\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{E}) = 1 \,( orall \mathbf{R} \in \mathrm{SO}(3))\). Also, this representation matrix adapts Condon-Shortley phase.

We define the action of a symmetry operation of the first kind on spinor as

\[ egin{aligned} \left[ (\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{v}) \mathbf{\Psi} ight] (\mathbf{r}) &:= \mathbf{U}( \mathbf{R} ) \mathbf{\Psi}( (\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{v})^{-1} \mathbf{r}) \ \Rightarrow \left[ g_{1} \left[ g_{2} \mathbf{\Psi} ight] ight](\mathbf{r}) &= \mathbf{U}(\mathbf{p}_{g_{1}}) \left[ g_{2} \mathbf{\Psi} ight](g_{1}^{-1}\mathbf{r}) \ &= z(\mathbf{p}_{g_{1}}, \mathbf{p}_{g_{2}}) \left[ (g_{1}g_{2}) \mathbf{\Psi} ight](\mathbf{r}). \end{aligned} \]

Consider Bloch function with \(\mathbf{k}\)

\[ egin{aligned} \mathbf{\Psi}_{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{r}) = e^{ i \mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{r} } \mathbf{u}_{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{r}), \end{aligned} \]

where \(\mathbf{u}_{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{r})\) is periodic w.r.t. lattice translations \(L_{\mathcal{T}}\). The Bloch function forms an irreps of translation subgroup \(\mathcal{T}\) of space group \(\mathcal{G}\):

\[ egin{aligned} (\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{t}) \mathbf{\Psi}_{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{r}) &= \mathbf{\Psi}( (\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{t})^{-1} \mathbf{r}) \ &= e^{ -i \mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{t} } \mathbf{\Psi}(\mathbf{r}) \quad (\mathbf{t} \in L_{\mathcal{T}}). \end{aligned} \]

A transformed Bloch function \((\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{v}) \mathbf{\Psi}_{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{r})\) is a Bloch function with \(\mathbf{Rk}\):

\[ egin{aligned} (\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{t}) (\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{v}) \mathbf{\Psi}_{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{r}) &= (\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{v}) (\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{R}^{-1}\mathbf{t}) \mathbf{\Psi}_{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{r}) \quad ( ecause z(\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{R}) = z(\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{E}) = 1 ) \ &= \exp \left( -i \mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{R}^{-1} \mathbf{t} ight) (\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{v}) \mathbf{\Psi}_{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{r}) \ &= \exp \left( -i \mathbf{Rk} \cdot \mathbf{t} ight) (\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{v}) \mathbf{\Psi}_{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{r}) \quad ( ecause \mathbf{R} \in \mathrm{SO}(3) ). \end{aligned} \]

Let \(\Gamma^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}\) be a projective irrep of the little group \(\mathcal{G}^{\mathbf{k}} = \coprod_{ \{ i \mid \mathbf{S}_{i} \in \overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}} \} } (\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{w}_{i}) \mathcal{T}\) and \(\{ \mathbf{\Psi}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}_{\mu} \}_{\mu=1}^{d_{\mathbf{k}\alpha}}\) form the projective irrep. For \(\mathbf{S}_{i} \mathbf{S}_{j} = \mathbf{S}_{k}\),

\[ egin{aligned} &\sum_{\mu} \mathbf{\Psi}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}_{\mu} \left[ \mathbf{\Gamma}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}((\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{w}_{i})) \mathbf{\Gamma}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}((\mathbf{S}_{j}, \mathbf{w}_{j})) ight]_{\mu u} \ &= (\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{w}_{i}) \left( (\mathbf{S}_{j}, \mathbf{w}_{j}) \mathbf{\Psi}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}_{ u} ight) \ &= rac{ z(\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{S}_{j}) }{ z(\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{S}_{k}) } (\mathbf{S}_{k}, \mathbf{w}_{k}) \left( (\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{S}_{k}^{-1} (\mathbf{S}_{i}\mathbf{w}_{j} + \mathbf{w}_{i} - \mathbf{w}_{k} ) ) \mathbf{\Psi}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}_{ u} ight) \ &= \sum_{\mu} \mathbf{\Psi}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}_{\mu} z(\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{S}_{j}) e^{-i\mathbf{k}\cdot \left( \mathbf{S}_{i}\mathbf{w}_{j} + \mathbf{w}_{i} - \mathbf{w}_{k} ight) } \mathbf{\Gamma}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}((\mathbf{S}_{k}, \mathbf{w}_{k})) \quad ( ecause z(\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{S}_{k}) = 1, \mathbf{S}_{k} \in \overline{\mathcal{G}}^{\mathbf{k}}). \end{aligned} \]

Then, Simplifying by

\[ egin{aligned} \mathbf{\Gamma}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}((\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{v})) &=: e^{ -i \mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{v} } \mathbf{D}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}((\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{v})) \ \mathbf{D}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}((\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{w}_{i})) \mathbf{D}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}((\mathbf{S}_{j}, \mathbf{w}_{j})) &= z(\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{S}_{j}) e^{ -i \mathbf{g}_{i} \cdot \mathbf{w}_{j} } \mathbf{D}^{\mathbf{k}\alpha}((\mathbf{S}_{k}, \mathbf{w}_{k})), \end{aligned} \]

where \(\mathbf{g}_{i} = \mathbf{S}_{i}^{-1} \mathbf{k} - \mathbf{k}\). We can enumerate projective irreps for spinor from the factor system \(\mu_{\mathbf{k}}(S_{i}, S_{j}) := z(\mathbf{S}_{i}, \mathbf{S}_{j}) \exp \left( -i \mathbf{g}_{i} \cdot \mathbf{w}_{j} ight)\).

items.title: Symmetry operation of the second kind
items.text:
We assume the inversion \(\mathbf{I}\) acts on spin functions as

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{I} \ket{\uparrow} &= \ket{\uparrow} \\ \mathbf{I} \ket{\downarrow} &= \ket{\downarrow}, \end{aligned} \]

which is known as Pauli gauge Altmann, 2005. In this convention, we can choose factor system as follows:

\[ \begin{aligned} z(\mathbf{I}, \mathbf{I}) &= 1 \\ z(\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{I}\mathbf{R}') &= z(\mathbf{IR}, \mathbf{R}') = z(\mathbf{IR}, \mathbf{I}\mathbf{R}') = z(\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{R}') \quad (\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{R}' \in \mathrm{SO}(3)). \end{aligned} \]

items.title: Convention of rotations for spinor
items.text:
A rotation \(\mathbf{R}_{ \theta\hat{\mathbf{n}} } \in \mathrm{SO}(3)\) can be written with angular momentum operators:

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{R}_{ \theta\hat{\mathbf{n}} } &= \exp \left( -i \theta \hat{\mathbf{n}} \cdot \mathbf{L} \right) \\ &= \begin{pmatrix} \cos \theta + n_{x}^{2} (1 - \cos \theta) & n_{x} n_{y} (1 - \cos \theta) - n_{z} \sin \theta & n_{x} n_{z} (1 - \cos \theta) + n_{y} \sin \theta \\ n_{y} n_{x} (1 - \cos \theta) + n_{z} \sin \theta & \cos \theta + n_{y}^{2} (1 - \cos \theta) & n_{y} n_{z} (1 - \cos \theta) - n_{x} \sin \theta \\ n_{z} n_{x} (1 - \cos \theta) - n_{y} \sin \theta & n_{z} n_{y} (1 - \cos \theta) + n_{x} \sin \theta & \cos \theta + n_{z}^{2} (1 - \cos \theta) \\ \end{pmatrix} \\ \mathbf{L}_{x} &:= -i \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ \end{pmatrix} \\ \mathbf{L}_{y} &:= -i \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ \end{pmatrix} \\ \mathbf{L}_{z} &:= -i \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \end{pmatrix} \\ \end{aligned} \]

The axis and angle of \(\mathbf{R}_{ \theta\hat{\mathbf{n}} }\) are interpret by the following relations:

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{R}_{f} &:= \mathbf{A}^{-1} \mathbf{R}_{ \theta\hat{\mathbf{n}} } \mathbf{A} \quad \in \mathrm{SL}(3) \\ \mathrm{tr} \mathbf{R}_{ \theta\hat{\mathbf{n}} } &= 2 \cos \theta + 1 \\ \end{aligned} \] \[ \begin{aligned} \begin{pmatrix} [R_{ \theta\hat{\mathbf{n}} }]_{23} - [R_{ \theta\hat{\mathbf{n}} }]_{32} \\ [R_{ \theta\hat{\mathbf{n}} }]_{31} - [R_{ \theta\hat{\mathbf{n}} }]_{13} \\ [R_{ \theta\hat{\mathbf{n}} }]_{12} - [R_{ \theta\hat{\mathbf{n}} }]_{21} \\ \end{pmatrix} = -2 (\sin \theta) \hat{\mathbf{n}} \end{aligned} \]

The corresponding unitary rotation is explicitly written as

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{U} ( \mathbf{R}_{ \theta\hat{\mathbf{n}} } ) &= \exp \left( -\frac{i}{2}\theta \hat{\mathbf{n}} \cdot \mathbf{\sigma} \right) \\ &= \mathbf{1} \cos \frac{\theta}{2} - i (\hat{\mathbf{n}} \cdot \mathbf{\sigma}) \sin \frac{\theta}{2} \\ &= \begin{pmatrix} \cos \frac{\theta}{2} - i n_{z} \sin \frac{\theta}{2} & (-i n_{x} - n_{y}) \sin \frac{\theta}{2} \\ (-i n_{x} + n_{y}) \sin \frac{\theta}{2} & \cos \frac{\theta}{2} + i n_{z} \sin \frac{\theta}{2} \\ \end{pmatrix}. \end{aligned} \]
